title: Bloom’s Taxonomy / Design Specification
subtitle: Intuit TurboTax-inspired Train-the-Trainer portfolio sample
status: High-fidelity design prototype; ready for Development planning, pending human design and instructional review

sections.title: 01 / Design intent
items: The experience

A trainer learns to connect thinking, objectives and evidence. A photographic introduction establishes the human learning context; task screens then give the activity, choice and feedback the visual priority.
Visual thesis

Bright editorial workspace: near-white canvas, dark ink, strong red emphasis and quiet borders. Large headings create a clear hierarchy; short paragraphs and purposeful whitespace keep the work readable.
Portfolio positioning

Based on Lorne’s stated Training and Quality Manager experience training trainers. Intuit TurboTax is the selected brand context. All scenarios are newly written, fictional and independent of actual employer training.
Scope

Twelve logical screens, six classification tasks, one authored objective, a five-item check, retry and completion states, resources and preferences. This is a browser design prototype, not a replacement for Adapt or a deployed LMS.

sections.title: 02 / Brand system
items: Identity
Plain-text Intuit TurboTax context label paired with Trainer Studio and an independent-portfolio disclosure. No recreated checkmark, official logo asset or endorsement claim.
Color roles

Primary #C8202F; hover #A71625; ink #172B32; muted #53636B; canvas #F5F7F8; surface #FFFFFF; control boundary #71828A; link/focus #174EA6; success #17643A. Red identifies primary action and emphasis; green is reserved for reviewed or correct states.
Typography

Arial / Helvetica / sans-serif makes the prototype portable without external font downloads. Body 18px desktop and 17px phone; learner task text approximately 16-20px; headings fluid from 34px to 75px. Secondary metadata is smaller and does not carry essential instructions. This replaces the Analysis working DejaVu typeface.
Spacing and form

An 8px-based rhythm with 18-32px panel padding. Main surfaces use 12-20px corners; the hero uses one asymmetric arch crop to distinguish the introduction. Controls use quieter 8-10px corners. Avoid applying the hero treatment to every panel.
Voice

Direct, practical and reassuring. Feedback states the reason and next action. Brand tone is informed by Intuit’s official TurboTax content-design guidance; palette values here are design approximations rather than official specifications.

sections.title: 03 / Hero and media direction
items: Hero concept

An adult trainer and two colleagues evaluate a learning activity in a bright studio. The red garment connects photography to the action color without adding logos. The people are generated illustrative subjects, not represented as actual Intuit employees.
Placement

Desktop: image on the right beside title, outcome, duration and Begin lesson. Mobile: title and primary action precede a wide photograph. The same asset returns at the wrap-up to connect the end of the learning experience to its opening.
Accessible meaning
The adjacent copy conveys the objective. The image has concise alternative text and contains no essential embedded instructions. All decisions remain usable with images unavailable.
Production asset
prototype/assets/trainer-hero.png; original 1536 x 1024 PNG, generated with the built-in image-generation tool. The full prompt is in Asset-Provenance.json. No video or narration has been recorded.
Motion

A 300ms content reveal and brief color transitions support orientation. Device reduced-motion settings suppress animation; an in-lesson option also removes interface motion. No timed or moving content is required to learn.

sections.title: 04 / Layout and navigation
items: Persistent structure

Identity and resources/preferences at top; a desktop lesson rail shows twelve steps and reviewed progress; a central reading/task area carries one screen heading. Back/Continue appear below each applicable task. Mobile replaces the rail with a labeled modal menu.
Responsive behavior

Desktop uses a 250px navigation rail, reduced to 220px at intermediate widths. Below 850px the rail becomes a menu; below 600px split tasks stack. The hero moves beneath its copy. Controls stay in reading order rather than requiring horizontal swipes.
Navigation states

Every content screen can be visited from the menu. Continue acknowledges a reviewed step. Diagnostic, classification and alignment activities require a submission before Continue. Final wrap-up lists missing requirements rather than pretending the learner has completed the sample.
Focus behavior

Screen changes move focus to the lesson heading. Modal dialogs close with Escape and return focus to the trigger. Feedback after a submitted answer is announced and receives focus, placing the keyboard user near the next action. This refines the Analysis feedback-focus proposal.
Resource layer

Resources includes an HTML checklist, a text-file download and reference links. Reading preferences offer larger lesson text and reduced motion. No audio toggle, search, certificate or login is displayed because those services are not implemented.

sections.title: 05 / Interaction contract
items: S01-S04: orient and explore

S01 launches the lesson. S02 requires one diagnostic choice, then explanatory feedback. S03 uses native expandable sections and Expand all / Collapse all. S04 presents the knowledge dimension as four readable examples. Content clicks alone are not treated as proof of learning.
S05-S07: model and practice

S05 highlights condition, action or standard and repeats the explanation in text. S06 requires all six classifications and preserves the first practice score across retries. S07 requires a choice and explains how judgment differs from recall or copying.
S08: write and review

Two text areas capture the objective and evidence. Four Yes / Needs revision self-ratings and a model response support revision. Continue requires both fields and all four self-ratings. The draft can be downloaded as UTF-8 text, or explicitly kept only in the tab.
S09-S10: check and review

Five question subpages preserve answers when going back. Explanations appear after final submission. Retry clears the five choices, increments the attempt, preserves the first result and displays the latest result. Results link to targeted content.
S11-S12: transfer and closure

The checklist and optional next-step reflection support transfer. Wrap-up distinguishes quiz result, draft self-review and lesson participation. It never claims that data reached an LMS or that a certification was earned.

sections.title: 06 / Evidence and scoring
items: Classification objective
Six-task practice target: at least 5/6 on first submission. Later practice scores can support revision but do not replace the first-attempt measure.
Alignment objective

Q3-Q5 measure alignment decisions. The objective target is 3/3. The overall knowledge-check target is separately 4/5 or 80%; a learner can pass the aggregate check while still needing alignment review.
Authored objective

The four criteria cover condition, action, standard and aligned evidence. The prototype records self-review only. A human reviewer must evaluate the draft to establish independent quality evidence; there is no semantic auto-grading.
Completion

All required lesson steps must be acknowledged or their required activities submitted. A passing knowledge-check score is not required for participation completion. Missing steps appear as direct links. Actual LMS status mapping will be implemented and tested in Development.
Prototype data

All state exists in JavaScript memory in the current tab. There is no browser storage, network telemetry, LMS identity or database. Refresh clears progress and text. Draft export is explicit. The download test uses fictional content only.

sections.title: 07 / Accessibility and usability
items: Built into the design

Semantic buttons, radios, labels, fieldsets, native select controls, expandable sections, dialog focus behavior, a skip link, explicit errors, text feedback and visible focus. No essential drag, hover, color-only meaning, autoplay or time limit.
Contrast and targets

White on primary red is approximately 5.67:1. Focus uses a high-contrast blue outline. Main buttons target at least 44px in height; radio options provide larger clickable label regions. Color-pair calculations and visible focus do not constitute a WCAG conformance audit.
Observed prototype checks

The accompanying QA report records the executed browser, interactions, scores, exports and responsive checks. Screenshots document actual rendered states. Only checks marked passed in that report are observed results.
Remaining validation

Manual screen-reader review, keyboard completion of every branch, 200% text/400% zoom evaluation, cross-browser Safari/Firefox checks and user testing remain. WCAG 2.2 AA is the production target, not a present certification.
Learner research

No participant interviews or usability pilot have been performed. Validate the conceptual distinctions and comprehension of feedback with novice trainers, then record revisions. Do not present test-run scores as learner results.

sections.title: 08 / Changes from Analysis
items: Visual direction expanded

The original low-fidelity board has become a photographic, responsive design. The user specifically requested hero imagery, modern interaction, color and stronger brand identity. The lesson scope and train-the-trainer context remain intact.
Title and screen copy refined

The course identity remains Bloom’s Taxonomy: Design Practice That Proves Learning. Great training. Visible learning. is the welcome headline. Screen text is tightened for reading; the meaning of objectives, keys and evidence is preserved.
Preferences bounded
Text remains the complete lesson. Audio, dark mode and a dyslexia-specific font are omitted rather than represented as inactive controls. Larger lesson text and reduced motion work in the prototype.
Draft departure clarified

Instead of requiring a destructive discard when leaving S08, the user may download or explicitly continue with the draft kept only in the tab. An unsaved-draft browser close warning is requested where supported; it is not a guarantee against data loss.
Persistence deferred honestly
Analysis described future resume and service acknowledgements. The prototype intentionally makes no persistence or save-to-LMS claim. Those states remain part of the production integration backlog.

sections.title: 09 / Development handoff
items: Reusable structure
The prototype source separates index.html, css/style.css, js/content.js, js/app.js and assets/. The one-file HTML is a review convenience. Do not treat it as the final production architecture.
Adapt translation

Map narrative content to Adapt text components, scenarios and scored items to suitable question components, and the six-process explorer to accessible accordion behavior. Implement the authored draft/rubric/export as a reviewed extension if no installed component meets the contract. Theme tokens belong in the Adapt theme.
LMS/LRS integration

The existing proof stack needs new answered/interacted/passed/failed events, registration and attempt data, authenticated identity, retry handling and actual browser completion. Keep secrets server-side and exclude objective text from telemetry. Follow the Analysis event contract before introducing dual tracking.
SCORM gate

Build through the existing Adapt/Spoor SCORM 1.2 route; import in Moodle and test launch, bookmark, score, lesson_status and resume. This design HTML contains no SCORM API adapter. Previously passed infrastructure tests are not proof of this lesson’s runtime compatibility.
Next work sequence

Human content/design review -> component mapping -> Adapt theme and lesson build -> question/draft behavior tests -> accessibility review -> Moodle/LRS integration -> small pilot -> publication. No changes to the existing infrastructure repositories were made by this design package.

sections.title: 10 / Decisions and readiness
items: Ready

A coherent visual system, original hero asset, twelve-screen interactive prototype, scored and remediation states, editable visual review deck, source-separated files and documented behavior are available for Development planning.
Not yet complete

Independent instructional review, learner validation, official-logo treatment if desired, screen-reader/cross-browser validation and production integrations. No training effectiveness or brand approval is claimed.
Review prompts

Can a trainer explain why a choice fits? Does the draft exercise make the intended judgment observable? Is the red accent reserved for meaningful emphasis? Can a learner recover from an error or unfinished step without losing orientation?
Release boundary

Do not publish as a certified or official employer course. Publish only after the intended hosting, tracking, privacy and accessibility behaviors are verified. Keep the independent portfolio context visible.
Sources

Analysis baseline v1.0; Carnegie Mellon Eberly Center taxonomy and alignment pages; W3C WCAG 2.2; Intuit Content Design TurboTax voice; Intuit official public identity references. See Source-Register.txt for direct links.
